chunks: My father (rah) said: Ahmad ibn Idris narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Ahmad narrated to me, saying: Amru ibn Ali narrated from his uncle Muhammad ibn Umar, who raised it to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
One who inscribes on his ring: 'Maashaa Allaahu, laa quwwata illaa billaahi, astaghfirullaah' will be safe from devastating poverty.
ai.seo_question: What is the reward of inscribing 'Maashaa Allaah' on one's ring?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Thawab al-A'mal*, this hadith highlights the Shia tradition of using physical objects as vessels for spiritual protection, linking the act of inscribing the ring with the triad of divine will, power, and forgiveness. The specific phrase 'Ma shaa' Allah la quwwata illa billah' emphasizes reliance on God's omnipotence, while the inclusion of 'Astaghfirullah' underscores the purifying effect of repentance in alleviating material and spiritual destitution. This practice reflects the broader Imami belief in the efficacy of *dhikr* and *dua* embedded in tangible forms to secure divine favor.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 1. My father (rah) said: it was narrated to me by Ahmad b. Idris who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ahmad who said it was narrated to me by ’Amru b. Ali from his uncle Muhammad b. Umar who raised it to Abi Abdillah (a.s.) who said: “
One who inscribes: Maashaa Allaahu laa quwwata illaa billaahi astaghfirullaah on his ring, will remain safe from devastating poverty.”
